messages.subject: Multilevel 2PL with discrimination parameters at the cluster level.
messages.subject_clean: Multilevel 2PL with discrimination parameters at the cluster level.
messages.body_plain:
Hi Phil,

I am currently trying to fit a multilevel 2PL model as presented in Sulis & Toland (2017) in the paper titled “Introduction to Multilevel Item Response Theory Analysis: Descriptive and Explanatory Models”.  The multilevel 2PL presented in this paper has two sets of discrimination parameter sets, one for each level (i.e., person and cluster).

I am wondering, is it possible to fit this model using the mixedmirt function? I’ve read the documentation and I find myself unable to define discrimination parameters at the cluster level.

At the moment, I have been able to fit a multilevel 2PL but only with one set of discrimination parameters at the person-level. For this model, I have used the following code:

model2 = "Theta = 1-25

                  START = (1, a1, 1)

                  FIXED = (1, a1)

                  FREE=(2-25,a1)

                  COV = Theta*Theta"

ml2pl <- mixedmirt(it, cov[, 1:2], model2,

                               fixed = ~ 0 + items,

                               lr.random = ~ 1|class,

                               itemtype = "2PL")

I am looking forward to hearing from you,

Best,

Sebastian

messages.subject: DIF testing with dichotomous and polytomous items
messages.subject_clean: DIF testing with dichotomous and polytomous items
messages.body_plain:
Dear Phil

First of all a huge thank you for mirt and the support and materials available, it is great and has helped me so much in my phd research!

I am currently redoing some DIF analysis I previously conducted and I am encountering a new error that I hadn't faced last time I ran this on the same data. I am testing for DIF with an item set that has mostly dichotomous items and a few polytomous items (0,1,2) so I've fitted the models with itemtype = 2PL for the dichotomous items and itemtype = gpcm for poly items.

Previously, after running a drop DIF I selected an anchor set and then for the second round of DIF testing I was running this code:
# Specify Itemtype
itemtype <- ifelse(max == 1, '2PL', 'gpcm')

# Constrained model 1 ----
conmod1 <- multipleGroup(items, 1, group=group, itemtype=itemtype,
                        invariance = c(colnames(items), 'free_means', 'free_var'))

# DIF test 1 ----
#The other items serve as the anchor items (i.e., the all-others-as-anchors model).
diftest <- DIF(conmod1, c('d','d1','d2'),
               scheme = 'drop', seq_stat = .01, p.adjust = 'fdr')

# select anchors from DIF free items in DIF test 1
# load anchor set and test set values
load("Rdata/ancset.RData") # anchor set
load("Rdata/testset.RData") # test set

# Specify a New constrained Model using Anchor Items ----
# Run model
ancmod <- multipleGroup(items, 1, group = group, itemtype = itemtype, SE=T,
                      invariance = c(ancset, 'free_means', 'free_var'))

# DIF test 2 : DIF detection LR Tests ----
diftest2 <- DIF(ancmod, c('d','d1', 'd2'), items2test = testset, p.adjust = 'fdr')
 Error in checkForRemoteErrors(val) :
  7 nodes produced errors; first error: 'i' and 'j' must not contain NA
Previously it ran with no problems, but now I am encountering an error when I run diftest2. At first I assumed it was an error is because the polytomous items didnt have a 'd' value and only have d1 and d2. So I attempted:
diftest2 <- DIF(ancmod, c('d'), items2test = testset, p.adjust = 'fdr')
  |++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++          | 80% ~03m 48s      Error in checkForRemoteErrors(val) :
  one node produced an error: 'i' and 'j' must not contain NA
and again encountered a similar error. Which makes me think the problem is likely to be the mix of poly and dichotmous items as there are either d or d1/d2 values marked as NA. However, I am not sure why I didn't face this error when I ran this same code a few months ago as there were still a mix of itemtypes then.

Do I need to test the 2PL and GPCM items separately for DIF after setting the anchor?

Do you have any suggestions or ideas of what might be occurring?

Happy to share more detailed code/data if it would be helpful.

Thank you again for the great package and helpful forum!

Best,
Heather

messages.subject: Compute M2/C2 statistics on datasets with non-random missing values
messages.subject_clean: Compute M2/C2 statistics on datasets with non-random missing values
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

I am working on a confirmatory factor analysis on a sparse-matrix (N=6000) with non-random missing values. The sparse-matrix has binary (0, 1) and polytomous (0, 1, 2, 3) response data and data is supposed to have one dimension.
The model is very simple, but I have trouble in calculating the fit statistics because of the missing values. Unfortunately, I cannot remove them or do any imputations.

Is it possible to calculate fit statistics like CFI, BIC, RMSEA and SRMR without removing any missing values?
If mirt cannot do it, are there any R packages that capable of doing it?

Thx!
Denise

messages.subject: Experimental design, longitudinal IRT
messages.subject_clean: Experimental design, longitudinal IRT
messages.body_plain:
Dear Phil,

First of all thanks for your help and work on the {mirt} package, it has really helped me with my research. I'm a master student and I'm currently attempting to conduct data analysis for my master's thesis in education. My supervisors know nothing about IRT and I have learnt everything about it on my own, so sorry in advance if I don't get some ideas right.

I have a database consisting of three groups (Control, Exp1, Exp2) where I have recorded different sociodemographic variables of the students and each of them has responded the same questionnaire twice (pre and post intervention). The questionnaire is based on a Likert scale (1-4) and includes 10 items. Thus, the database looks something like this (with more students (N=682), sociodemographic variables and pre-post items):

ID Group Socdem1 Socdem2 Socdem3 PreItem1 PreItem2 PostItem1 PosItem2

1      Cont              1             2             3             1             2             2             1

2      Cont              1             2             2             1             2             1             1

3      Exp1              1             1             2             3             2             1             3

4      Exp1              2             1             1             4             3             4             4

5      Exp2              2             2             1             4             3             3             4

6      Exp2              1             1             2             4             4             4             4

The thing is I would like to estimate each students' ability through fitting PCMs in order to compare how each students' ability changes depending on the group, the time-point and the sociodemographic variables. However, I don't know which is the most suitable approach to it.

The winstep rasch webpage (https://www.rasch.org/rmt/rmt171a.htm) suggests racking (it is already racked right now) and stacking the data in order to: 1) test the differential impact of the interventions on the items; and 2) tests the differential impact of the intervention on the persons' ability respectively. Nevertheless, based on what I have read both in the package and the google group, I'm not sure whether the mirt package supports this approach.

Therefore, what should I do with this multiple group longitudinal data? Should I just fit a baseline PCM (pre data) without considering the cohort groups and estimate students' pre and post ability using that model's item parameters? Should I fit the models using multiplegroup()? Or should I use a different approach without estimating students' individual abilities?

Sorry for the long post, and thanks in advance. I am really lost with this and the only question with a similar doubt is unanswered in the group (https://groups.google.com/g/mirt-package/c/WGipKilug-I/m/_km_Q0MoCgAJ).

-John

messages.subject: M2 based fit indices in discrete mirt
messages.subject_clean: M2 based fit indices in discrete mirt
messages.body_plain:
Hello.
I estimated very basic LCA model (with binary items and two categories) using mdirt function, for example as fit <- mdirt(data, 2), here all data variables were binary.

Then I estimated model fit using M2 function (M2(fit)), which returned M2 statistics and df, p, and RMSEA with CI. First of all, M2 doesn't estimate null model, and thus doesn't return CFI and TLI. Second, it doesn't return SRMSR; if I asked for residual matrices (M2(fit, residmat = T)), it returns strange list with Xi2, delta, estpars, p, e, and SRMSR (which is NULL) objects.
First of all, why  isn't SRMSR estimated? Its construction should be the same as with traditional IRT (e.g., 2PL) model, or I am wrong?
Second, what are these objects which are returned as residual matrices? Why they have 21 rows/columns (6 items per 2 categories, 2 latent classes)?
And finally, I don't understand why the null model is not defined. It should be equivalent to the NULL model in 2PL model. I assume I can estimate null model as LCA model with a single group (i.e., fit <- mdirt(data, 1)), get M2 statistic and d.f., and estimate it manually. However, I am afraid this not to be the right approach; otherwise, I suppose it were already implemented.
Thank you for any advice!

(My data are special-education test with recognition of the first and last phone in a word. Therefore, children either can or cannot discriminate phones, which lead to bimodal distribution of raw scores, perfect 2PL model fit, and alpha > .98 even with five or six items. On the other hand, it makes no sense to estimate 2PL model, if I see this pattern; at least its parameters would be biased. However, the LCA model is still slightly worse compared to 2PL and I need complete fit indices to report in test manual.)

However, I am afraid this not to be the right approach; otherwise, I suppose it were already implemented.

messages.subject: DIF & empirical_ES vs DRF?
messages.subject_clean: DIF & empirical_ES vs DRF?
messages.body_plain:
Dear Phil

Thank you again for your package and support on this forum.

I have been running DIF analysis for my phd (in various iterations and formats) and settled on using mirt::DIF() and then quantifying the item-level effect size using Meade's (2010) taxonomy (predominantly SIDS, UIDS and ESSD).

I am now looking at bundle and test level impact of DIF and I have recently come across your 2023 IRT-Based Effect Sizes for DIF Investigations paper. I have been playing around with the DRF function using sDRF and uDRF as effect size indices for the bundle and test level impact. I am really enjoying their interpretability and your paper has been very helpful to understand the differences between the effect size index options, thank you! They are also particularly useful as the groups I am comparing have quite different ability distributions so it is great to be able to look at restricted ranges of theta.

However, I am now questioning if you would recommend DRF for item-level analyses too (instead of the combination of DIF and empirical ES)? My main concern with using DRF() is there are a lot of items in the test I am analysing and so I have been using a BH adjusted p-value to flag DIF, and I cannot see an option to include an adjusted p-value when using DRF.

Any advice or comments would be thoroughly appreciated.

With thanks,
Heather

messages.subject: Question regarding the impute argument in older mirt version
messages.subject_clean: Question regarding the impute argument in older mirt version
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

I am currently working through an example from the "Handbook of Educational Measurement and Psychometrics Using R" by Desjardins and Bulut. The example pertains to item fit of a Rasch model using the mirt package.

Their R code was:

rasch_itemfit <- itemfit(rasch_fit,
fit_stats = c("S_X2", "G2"),
impute = 10)
head(rasch_itemfit)

This results in:

item        G2      df.G2   p.G2    S_X2    df.S_X2  p.S_X2
1 reason.4   10.888   9     0.344   20.597  12       0.057
2 reason.16  9.007    9     0.443   10.802  12       0.546
3 reason.17  15.409   9     0.131   19.920  12       0.069
4 reason.19  14.018   9     0.166   26.702  12       0.009
5 letter.7   5.458    9     0.788   12.490  12       0.407
6 letter.33  14.195   9     0.163   27.096  13       0.012

However, when I run the same code, I encounter the following error message:

Only X2, G2, PV_Q1, PV_Q1*, infit, X2*, and X2*_df can be computed with missing data.
Pass na.rm=TRUE to remove missing data row-wise

I understand that something has changed regarding the impute argument in the mirt package since the book was published. How can I recreate their results with the current version of the mirt package? Should I use imputeMissing or a different function?

Cheers,
Oskar

messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I want to use the mirtCAT function to run a simulation study. When setting the stopping criteria , if I add delta_thetas=0.05, the test will terminate after only one item. Do you know where the problem is?

Thank you for any advice!

My code is as follows :

set.seed(1957)

np <- 10000
testlength <- 98
itemnames <- paste0("Item.", 1: testlength)
TL <- 49

d <- item.params$items[, c("d1", "d2", "d3", "d4", "d5")]
d_params <- as.matrix(d)

a <- item.params$items[, c("a1", "a2", "a3", "a4", "a5", "a6", "a7")]
a_params <- as.matrix(a)

mod2 <- generate.mirt_object(parameters, itemtype = 'graded', latent_covariance = random_cov_matrix)

design3 = list(min_SEM = c(0.4,0.4,0.4,0.4,0.4,0.4,0.4), delta_thetas=0.05, max_items = 98)

Trule_mcat <- mirtCAT(mo = mod2, local_pattern = simulated_data , method = 'MAP', criteria = "Trule", design = design3)

Best regards,
Becca
